name: git-guard
what: Git commands that discard work or sweep up another agent's files in a shared repository are refused, while commands that name their paths pass.

faults.fault: git add . is no longer treated as staging everything.
git reset --hard is no longer recognised, because the flag is misspelled in the check.
The branch-name match loses its end anchor, so pushing a branch such as main-fix is refused.
The paths after git stash are not read, so git stash push src/a.js is refused like a bare stash.
A forced push is only caught when the long flag is used, so -f slips through.
A launcher's flag values are no longer skipped, so the user name after sudo -u is read as the command and the git command behind it goes unchecked.
eval is no longer unpacked, so a command passed to eval goes unchecked.
The PowerShell tool is no longer inspected, so git add -A passes there.
The checked-out branch is ignored, so a bare git push from main is allowed.
Every push without a refspec is treated as a push of the checked-out branch even when the refspec names another branch.
A dry run of git clean is no longer recognised, so git clean -nfd is refused.
A sweep flag refuses every git add even when paths are named, so git add -A src/a.js is blocked.
git add -u and -uv are no longer treated as a sweep of every tracked change.
A git stash with no named path is allowed, so git stash push sweeps up everyone's changes.
git stash push . is allowed, because a whole-directory path is no longer seen as a sweep.
The value of git stash -m is read as a path, so git stash push -m note passes as if it named a file.
A cd earlier in the command is ignored, so a bare push from a feature branch is judged by the session's folder.
An input redirection reads as a named path, so git add -A </dev/null passes.
